html:
A series of agreements between the United States and Mexico, from 1942 to 1964, that brought Mexican men to work on US farms and railways on short contracts. "Bracero" means a manual labourer, one who works with his arms.

It began during World War II, when US farms were short of workers. Over its 22 years it issued about 4.6 million contracts, many to the same men returning year after year. Workers were promised fair wages, housing and food. In practice many faced poor housing, health checks with harsh chemical spraying at the border, and pay below the promise. Part of their wages was held back for savings that many never received.

The program shaped migration for decades. It created networks linking Mexican villages to American farms, and many workers came without papers alongside it. Growers fought to keep it, while unions and civil rights groups opposed it. After it ended in 1964, labour leaders such as César Chávez were able to organise farm workers.
sum: A series of agreements between the United States and Mexico, from 1942 to 1964, that brought Mexican men to work on US farms and railways on short contracts. "Bracero" means a manual labourer, one who works with his arms.
